title: Why three reasonable fairness definitions cannot all be true
question: Why three reasonable fairness definitions cannot all be true
hook: ProPublica said COMPAS was biased; its maker said it was fair — and both were arithmetically correct.
core_idea: Bayes' rule ties precision to base rate times the error-rate ratio, so enforcing calibrated scores across groups with different base rates forces their error rates apart — a four-line theorem, not a tooling gap.
visual_object: the odds identity v/(1−v) = p/(1−p) · t/f as a balance whose base-rate weight, once moved, forces the error-rate side to tilt
exclusions: no demographic-parity extension, no Kleinberg three-way proof, no COMPAS history beyond one line, no debiasing toolkit
